text:
1. The passage presents the three days of travel as a kind of suspended sentence.
2. During the three days of travel, nothing outward happens, yet everything of significance happens.
3. The text emphasizes the servants, the wood, the knife, and the fire.
4. By emphasizing these items, the text names the instruments of the act before the act itself occurs.
5. The story holds obedience and horror together at the same time.
6. The story never lets either obedience or horror prevail over the other.
7. In this story, faith is a structured relationship or arrangement rather than a feeling.
8. Comparing this scene with the earlier promise reduces the apparent difference between them.
9. The chapter reminds the reader that Isaac is the child of the covenant.
10. Isaac is the one through whom the nations are to be blessed.
11. The chapter turns the covenant promise into a test.
12. The scene hinges on the single word "hineni."
13. "Hineni" means "here I am."
14. Abraham says "hineni" three times.
15. Abraham says "hineni" once to God, once to Isaac, and once to the angel.
16. Each time Abraham says "hineni," the word means something different.
17. Each successive time Abraham says "hineni," it costs him more.
18. In this story, the language of being present is also the language of loss.
